title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the proof of Proposition 1 from p.1 of 'Algèbre des figures' (GF V, 'Sorites ensemblistes', 14.6.86).

Setting: L is a set and 𝔏 ⊂ 𝔓(L) is a family of subsets. Grothendieck defines:
- |𝔏| = ∪_{A∈𝔏} A;
- ∂A = ∪{B∈𝔏 : B ⊊ A};
- A° = A∖∂A, the 'open stratum' or 'interior' of A;
- 𝔏' = {A : A° ≠ ∅}.

The proposition says three conditions are equivalent:
- (1°) For every point x, the family 𝔏_x = {A ∈ 𝔏 : x ∈ A} has a smallest element A(x), the 'carrier' of x.
- (2°) Two conditions hold:
  - (α) A∩B is the union of the members of 𝔏 contained in A∩B;
  - (β) every x ∈ |𝔏| lies in some A°, i.e. 𝔏_x has minimal elements.
- (3°) Three conditions hold:
  - (γ) the A°, A∈𝔏', partition |𝔏|;
  - (δ) each A∈𝔏 is saturated for that partition, i.e. is a union of strata;
  - (η) if A°⊂B and A°≠∅ then A⊂B (a 'frontier condition').

Proof on this page:
- (1°⇒2°), α: for x∈A∩B, the carrier C = A(x) satisfies x ∈ C ⊂ A∩B.
- (1°⇒2°), β: A(x) is minimal in 𝔏_x, i.e. x ∈ A(x)°.
- (2°⇒3°), key lemma: if x∈A° then A is the smallest element of 𝔏_x. Take B ∋ x. By α, x lies in some C∈𝔏 with C ⊂ A∩B. Since x∈A°, C cannot be strictly smaller than A, so C = A and hence A ⊂ B.
- From the lemma: γ follows, since two strata containing x are both the smallest element of 𝔏_x. δ follows, since the stratum B° through x∈A has B ⊂ A. η follows directly.
- (3°⇒1°): for x∈|𝔏|, let A be the unique element with x∈A°. If B∋x, then δ gives A°⊂B, and η gives A⊂B. So A = A(x).

In modern terms, the proposition characterises families of 'closed cells' such that every point has a smallest closed cell (its carrier). Equivalently, the family induces a decomposition into strata A° with the frontier condition: each closed set is a union of strata, and a closure contains every stratum it meets. This is the combinatorial skeleton of a CW/stratified decomposition, and of the specialization preorder of an Alexandrov topology. It is preparatory set-theoretic groundwork ('sorites') for an 'algebra of figures', apparently in the spirit of a combinatorial or tame geometry of polyhedral figures. The next page calls such families 'pré-admissibles'.
errors: Condition 1° is stated 'pour tout x ∈ L'. Literally this fails for x ∉ |𝔏|, where 𝔏_x is empty. It should read x ∈ |𝔏|, or one assumes |𝔏| = L. Likewise β on p.1 is written '∀x ∈ 𝔏' where '∀x ∈ |𝔏|' is meant.
In γ the proof says 'A minimal dans A', which must mean 'minimal dans 𝔏_x'. This is a slip, not a mathematical error.
Otherwise the proof is correct and complete. The lemma 'x∈A° ⇒ A = A(x)' under α is the key step and is correctly argued.

ideas.what: Equivalence between 'every point has a smallest member of 𝔏 containing it' and 'the interiors A° = A∖∂A partition |𝔏|, each A is a union of strata, and a closure containing a point of a stratum contains the whole closed cell'.
ideas.modern_name: Carrier of a point in a cell/stratified decomposition; frontier condition; Alexandrov (finite-space) specialization preorder; face-poset description of regular cell complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (CW complexes: Whitehead 1949; Alexandrov spaces: P. S. Alexandrov 1937; stratifications: Whitney/Thom)
ideas.where_published: Not in this set-theoretic form. Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology and stratifications only informally.

ideas.what: Lemma: under α, x ∈ A° implies A is the smallest element of 𝔏_x.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, routine set-theoretic lemma (Grothendieck's own heading is 'sorites') characterising cell-like decompositions by the existence of carriers. Its interest is purely as groundwork for the unpublished 'Algèbre des figures' (GF) project of 1986. The page contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'que $A$ est minimal dans $A$ [?]' should read 'que $A$ est minimal dans $\mathfrak{L}_x$'.
'on a vu de voir que [?]' is most likely 'on vient de voir que'.
The struck-through fragment in γ reads roughly '$x\in A^\circ \Rightarrow A$ plus petit élt de' before being replaced by 'i.e. A minimal dans 𝔏_x, i.e. que A est un plus petit élément de 𝔏_x'.
'3°⇒1°. Comme suivant [?] γ), et δ)': the intended sense is that γ and δ (together with η) are used to prove 1°. The opening word is illegible; 'Comme suivant' is doubtful.
The final line 'Par η), on a A⊂B' is correct; a struck line before it reads 'Il faut donc prouver que A°...'.
